node-1.label: The patient developed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules on the upper limbs and body

node-2.label: The patient was diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma the previous year and received 2 courses of radiotherapy to the head and leg and 4 cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed, and bevacizumab followed by nivolumab (3 mg/kg) every 2 weeks

node-3.label: After 8 cycles of nivolumab over 5 months, the papules appeared on the upper limbs, then spread to the rest of the body over the next 3 months, and the patient subsequently developed pruritus

node-4.label: Physical examination showed multiple 1- to 2-mm shiny papules scattered on the upper limbs and body, with lesions on the untreated arm coalescing into plaques

node-5.label: Immune-related cutaneous adverse reaction from nivolumab

attrs.why: The skin biopsy showing focal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates with vacuolar interface changes and melanin incontinence is characteristic of immune-related lichenoid dermatitis, directly supporting the diagnosis of immune-related cutaneous adverse reaction from nivolumab. Both the Laboratory Physician and Pathologist analyses confirm this histopathological pattern and rule out cutaneous metastasis. The temporal link and clinical morphology further consolidate the diagnosis, so confidence is raised from 0.75 to 0.9.

The biopsy findings of lymphohistiocytic infiltrates with interface changes and melanin incontinence, with no atypical epithelioid nests or intracytoplasmic mucin, provide histopathological evidence against cutaneous metastasis. Both expert analyses explicitly state that cutaneous metastasis is histologically unsupported. Although the patient has known metastatic lung adenocarcinoma, the absence of metastatic features in the biopsy and the ongoing immunotherapy context reduce confidence from 0.2 to 0.05.

node-4 supports presence of skin lesions but lacks specific infectious features; node-3 (pruritus) could fit benign conditions, but no evidence directly supports infection; low likelihood given cancer/immunotherapy context.

node-8.label: Skin biopsy shows focal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates with vacuolar interface changes and melanin incontinence

node-9.label: Skin biopsy shows no atypical epithelioid cell nests or intracytoplasmic mucin

node-10.label: Immune-related lichenoid dermatitis induced by nivolumab

attrs.why: The biopsy reveals focal lymphohistiocytic infiltrates beneath a thinned epidermis with vacuoles at the dermoepidermal junction and melanin incontinence, characteristic of interface dermatitis and consistent with an immune-related lichenoid reaction. The temporal link between nivolumab use and lesion onset, along with the clinical morphology of inflammatory papules coalescing into plaques, supports this specific subtype of immune-related cutaneous adverse reaction. Both the Laboratory Physician and Pathologist analyses confirm this diagnosis, so confidence is set at 0.85.
